details:
**Imran Khan**
A former captain of Pakistan's national cricket team and ICC Cricket Hall of Famer who founded the PTI (Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf) party. He lost the 2013 election, won in 2018, and served as prime minister until he was ousted by a no-confidence vote in 2022 and succeeded by Shehbaz Sharif. Since then he has faced a string of criminal cases, including contempt of court charges, and has been jailed.

**Islamabad**
Pakistan's capital, a planned city in the north of the country that replaced Karachi as the seat of government in the 1960s. It is the most common giveaway in tossups on Pakistan.

**Kashmir (Jammu and Kashmir)**
A Himalayan region that Pakistan and its neighbor India have fought over since partition in 1947. Both countries claim it, and it has been the cause of several wars and many border clashes.

**Balochistan**
Pakistan's largest province by area, in the southwest, and the site of a long-running separatist insurgency. The Balochistan Liberation Army (BLA), associated with figures such as Hyrbyair Marri, is one of the main militant groups there, and a 2022 military helicopter crash in the province killed six people.

**2022 Sindh floods**
Catastrophic monsoon flooding that began in June 2022 and was worst in the southern province of Sindh. The floods killed well over a thousand people and put roughly a third of the country under water. Later flooding in eastern Punjab province forced the evacuation of about 100,000 people.

**Cipher case and Donald Lu**
Imran Khan claimed that a diplomatic cable (the "cipher") describing a meeting with U.S. Assistant Secretary of State Donald Lu proved an American plot to remove his government. He was later charged with mishandling the classified cable, held in Attock Jail, and questioned over the missing copy.

**Toshakhana case**
A corruption case over gifts given to Imran Khan as prime minister, which are supposed to be deposited in the state gift repository (the Toshakhana). He was accused of selling some of them for profit, most famously a Graff watch given to him by Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman. His conviction in this case in 2023 led to his first imprisonment.

**Al-Qadir Trust case and May 9 "Black Day"**
Pakistan's anti-corruption agency, the National Accountability Bureau (NAB), arrested Imran Khan in May 2023 over a land and charity deal involving the Al-Qadir Trust. His supporters rioted on May 9 and attacked military buildings, a day the government called "Black Day." Chief Justice Umar Ata Bandial's Supreme Court soon declared the arrest unlawful, and Khan briefly went back to his Lahore home at Zaman Park.

**Nawaz Sharif and the 2013 election**
Nawaz Sharif's party, the Pakistan Muslim League (N), the "N" party, won the 2013 general election, which made him prime minister for a third time. It was the first time in Pakistan's history that one civilian government that had served a full term handed power to another. During the campaign Imran Khan was badly hurt when he fell off a forklift lifting him onto a stage at a rally in Lahore.

**Zulfikar Ali Bhutto and "eat grass"**
As foreign minister, Bhutto declared that Pakistanis would "eat grass" if necessary to build an atomic bomb to match India's. He resigned over Ayub Khan's signing of the 1966 Tashkent Agreement, which ended the 1965 war with India, then founded the PPP and led Pakistan after East Pakistan became independent as Bangladesh in 1971.

**Ahmadiyya declared non-Muslims**
In 1974, under pressure from clerics, Zulfikar Ali Bhutto's government passed a constitutional amendment declaring members of the Ahmadiyya religious movement to be non-Muslims. Ahmadis have faced legal discrimination and persecution in Pakistan ever since.

**Fatima Jinnah and "Basic Democracy"**
The sister of Pakistan's founder, Muhammad Ali Jinnah, she ran against military ruler Ayub Khan in the 1965 presidential election. Under Ayub's "Basic Democracy" system, the president was chosen by an electoral college of local councillors rather than by direct popular vote, and Ayub won.

**Asif Ali Zardari and "Memogate"**
Zardari, the widower of Benazir Bhutto, was president of Pakistan from 2008 to 2013 and again from 2024. Memogate was a 2011–2012 scandal over an unsigned memo sent to U.S. Admiral Mike Mullen asking for American help against a feared military coup. Pakistan's ambassador to the U.S., Husain Haqqani, was accused of being behind it and resigned.

**Salala incident and Shamsi Airbase**
In November 2011, NATO airstrikes on Pakistani border posts near the Afghan border killed about two dozen Pakistani soldiers. Pakistan responded by closing NATO supply routes and ordering the United States to leave Shamsi Airbase, which the CIA had used for drone operations. At the time, U.S. politicians such as Rick Perry questioned American aid to Pakistan, which was meant in part to curb the Haqqani network.

**Record heat in May 2022**
During a severe South Asian heat wave in May 2022, cities in Sindh such as Jacobabad, often called one of the hottest cities on Earth, reached temperatures around 50°C (over 120°F). The heat wave came just before that year's devastating floods.
